caption:
OpenAI says its latest models got much better at COBOL, Fortran and Visual Basic, the old languages banks and governments still run on.
On OpenAI's own COBOL migration test, GPT-6.1 Sol scored 86.6%, up from 5.4%, and 97.9% at higher effort.
OpenAI says experts still need to review and test the code.

slides.headline: OpenAI's AI just learned the 67-year-old code that *runs your ATM*

slides.heading: From *5.4%* to 86.6%
paras: OpenAI says its newest models got far better at COBOL, Fortran and Visual Basic, languages that banks, governments and businesses still depend on.
On its COBOL migration test, GPT-6.1 Sol scored 86.6% at low effort, up from 5.4% for GPT-5.6 Sol. At higher effort it reached 97.9%.

slides.heading: The code behind *your bank*
paras: COBOL dates back to 1959. OpenAI cites estimates that it supports more than 40% of online banking systems and 95% of ATM transactions.
Fortran still runs weather forecasting and nuclear reactor safety analysis. The pool of engineers who know these languages keeps shrinking.
slides.note: An IBM z17 mainframe, the kind of machine that still runs COBOL.

slides.hook: Old code still moves the world's money, and AI just learned to read it. Follow for what changes next.
